title: Cipher and Autopsy
premise: True-crime podcaster Cyrus Villalobos is hired by a nervous stranger who insists that a murder scheduled to happen in the coastal town of Marrow Bay must be prevented — a murder tied to the town's coldest case, the 1994 disappearance of a girl named Ada Quill. As Cyrus digs into thirty-year-old alibis, she discovers the town's founding families built their fortunes on covering up what happened to Ada, and that her client is one of them trying to stop history repeating. The climax comes when the tide recedes and gives up Ada's remains along with evidence implicating the current mayor; Cyrus must choose between broadcasting the truth — which will destroy the man she has come to love, the mayor's son — or burying it. She broadcasts it, justice arrives outside the law as the town itself turns on its patriarchs, and she leaves Marrow Bay with the case finally closed and her heart deliberately broken.
about_author: Paloma Sterling is a former court stenographer from the Pacific Northwest who spent a decade transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. Her novels are known for procedural precision braided with tidal, atmospheric dread.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Cyrus Villalobos, POV. A cash-stuffed envelope arrives with no return address and a single typed line: 'Stop the murder before it happens.' Cyrus, three years deep into her podcast about Ada Quill's 1994 disappearance, takes the meeting out of professional hunger. Emotional beat: wary curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. She reviews her archive of Marrow Bay interviews and realizes her anonymous client quoted phrasing only an insider would know. She maps the old alibis — four families, four identical stories about the night Ada vanished. Beat: the thrill of a pattern emerging.

chapters.title: Low Tide at Cutter's Point
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Following the client's cryptic coordinates, she walks the flats below Cutter's Point where Ada was last seen and finds fresh tire tracks and a buried tarp. Someone else knows the tide keeps secrets. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Mayor's Son
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Investigating the Quill family's old neighbors, she encounters Elias Marsh, the mayor's son, who runs the marina and remembers Ada fondly. Their chemistry is immediate and inconvenient. Beat: warmth intruding on suspicion.

chapters.title: Four Identical Stories
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. She re-interviews the aging patriarchs of the founding families and catches a rehearsed detail all four repeat word for word: the time the fog rolled in. Beat: cold certainty that this was coordinated.

chapters.title: What the Client Knows
chapters.summary: Anonymous client, POV (letters/recordings). The client reveals fragments: they were a child in 1994, they saw something on the beach, and the 'future murder' involves someone preparing to silence the last witness. Beat: guilt and terror.

chapters.title: Elias Alibi
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Elias offers his father's alibi for the night Ada vanished — a fishing trip with two witnesses now dead. He defends the mayor too easily, and Cyrus notes the flinch. Beat: attraction complicated by doubt.

chapters.title: The Podcast Goes Loud
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. She airs an episode teasing new evidence, and within hours her studio is broken into, her tapes rifled but nothing stolen — a message, not a theft. Beat: fear becoming defiance.

chapters.title: Ada's Sister Speaks
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Ada's estranged sister, dying of cancer, admits Ada was pregnant in 1994 and that the father belonged to one of the four families. Beat: grief cracking open the case's sealed heart.

chapters.title: A Murder Scheduled
chapters.summary: Client, POV. The client identifies the intended victim: the last living witness, an old boatman named Ferro, who has begun talking. The murder is set for the spring equinox tide. Beat: countdown pressure begins.

chapters.title: Guarding Ferro
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. She moves Ferro to a motel under a thin pretext and stakes out the marina, catching a figure photographing his door — a man on the mayor's payroll. Beat: protective resolve hardening.

chapters.title: Elias Confronted
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. She shows Elias the payroll ledger page; he goes pale and asks for forty-eight hours, refusing to explain. She lets him go and hates herself for it. Beat: love against duty, first fracture.

chapters.title: The Fog Story Collapses
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cross-referencing weather records, she proves the famous fog never rolled in that night — the shared alibi is physically impossible. All four families lied together. Beat: triumphant, terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Marina
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus is lured onto Elias's boat by a forged note and nearly run down in the channel; she survives but can't prove who sent it. Beat: trust shattered, paranoia total.

chapters.title: The Client Unmasked
chapters.summary: Client/Cyrus, alternating. The client reveals themselves: the mayor's younger brother, hidden away since 1994, the child who saw the burial. The 'murder yet to happen' is the mayor silencing him next. Beat: pity entwined with horror.

chapters.title: Equinox Eve
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. The eve of the equinox: Ferro disappears from the motel, the brother goes silent, and the mayor announces a marina dedication ceremony timed exactly with the low tide. Beat: coiled anticipation.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. At the ceremony, the record-low tide exposes Ada's remains and a rusted toolbox holding her diary naming her child's father: the mayor himself, then nineteen. Beat: the past surfacing in public, unstoppable.

chapters.title: Ferro Found Alive
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus traces Ferro to a beached skiff, wounded but alive, having refused to recant. His testimony plus the diary breaks the town open. Beat: exhausted relief, justice stirring outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: Elias's Choice
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. Elias confronts his father, learns he helped stage the 1994 cover-up as a terrified teenager, and chooses to hand the DA the family ledgers, ending the Marsh dynasty and any future with Cyrus. Beat: duty devouring love.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus airs the finale episode live as the mayor is arrested on the courthouse steps, reading Ada's diary aloud over the airwaves while the town listens in cars and kitchens. Beat: catharsis through truth-telling.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Alphabetized
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Weeks later: indictments land, the podcast ends its run, and Cyrus files the last tape. Elias leaves a letter she doesn't answer yet. Beat: quiet mourning for what justice cost.

chapters.title: The Next Envelope
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. On her last morning in Marrow Bay, a new envelope arrives — different handwriting, same advance payment, another town's secret. She looks at the sea, then pockets it. Beat: bittersweet renewal; the work, like the tide, never stops.
